aiAnalysisRun.findingsPreview: CONC 7.20.1R(2)(a): firm must notify the borrower as soon as possible of the missed payment and of any unpaid sums that have become payable.

claims.text: CONC 7.20.1R(2)(a): firm must notify the borrower as soon as possible of the missed payment and of any unpaid sums that have become payable.
CONC 7.20.1R(2)(b): firm must provide the borrower with sufficient information on the relevant agreement, adverse consequences (actual and likely) and, where relevant, mitigation steps.
CONC 7.20.1R(3): the information required under CONC 7.20.1R(2) must be provided together.

candidates.citation: PDF p.95 · legal instrument (FCA 2026/2, Annex F, CONC 7.20.1R(2)(a))
candidates.statement: Following a missed payment under a regulated deferred payment credit agreement, the firm must, as soon as possible, notify the borrower that the missed payment has occurred and about any sums that have become payable under the agreement but remain unpaid (including unpaid charges for non-compliance with the agreement).
candidates.sourceQuotation: As soon as possible after a missed payment has occurred the firm must: (a) notify the borrower: (i) that the missed payment has occurred; and (ii) about any sums which have become payable under the regulated deferred payment credit agreement but remain unpaid (including unpaid charges for non-compliance with the agreement)
candidates.applicabilityConditions: Applies where a borrower has failed to make a payment by the time it has fallen due under the terms of a regulated deferred payment credit agreement (a 'missed payment'), per CONC 7.20.1R(1). 'Payment' refers to repayment of capital and excludes payment of a charge for non-compliance with the agreement (CONC 7.20.1R(4)). Timing ('as soon as possible') requires firm judgement. The instrument is made (FCA 2026/2); commencement date derived from the supplied provisionLegal evidence (clause H). Draft recommendation requiring human review.

candidates.citation: PDF p.95 · legal instrument (FCA 2026/2, Annex F, CONC 7.20.1R(2)(b))
candidates.statement: Following a missed payment, the firm must, as soon as possible, provide the borrower with sufficient information for the borrower to understand: which agreement the missed payment relates to; any adverse consequences arising out of the missed payment; any adverse consequences the firm considers likely to arise; and, where relevant, any steps the borrower can take to mitigate those consequences.
candidates.sourceQuotation: (b) provide the borrower with sufficient information for the borrower to understand: (i) which regulated deferred payment credit agreement the missed payment relates to; (ii) any adverse consequences for the borrower arising out of the missed payment; (iii) any adverse consequences for the borrower that the firm considers are likely to arise out of the missed payment; and (iv) (where relevant) any steps the borrower can take to mitigate those adverse consequences.
candidates.applicabilityConditions: Applies where there is a missed payment under a regulated deferred payment credit agreement (CONC 7.20.1R(1)); 'payment' means repayment of capital, excluding charges for non-compliance (CONC 7.20.1R(4)). Step (iv) applies only where relevant. Sufficiency of information, scope of adverse consequences, the firm's view of likely consequences and relevance of mitigation steps involve firm judgement; CONC 7.20.2G (guidance, not binding) indicates firms should consider charges for missed payments and credit reference agency reporting. Draft recommendation requiring human review.

limitations: HARD_INVOICE_CAP_NOT_GUARANTEED: the shared ledger reserves the maximum estimated cost and later reconciles reported tokens. It is not an Anthropic invoice or workspace cap.

Pricing uses the static published list prices in MODEL_PRICING_ESTIMATE (version recorded per row). Standard input, output, cache writes (5m/1h) and cache reads are priced separately. Actual Anthropic invoices may differ (discounts, taxes, tiers).

A crashed instance can leave a RESERVED row. Recover it only with release_abandoned_lab_ai_reservation: a registered operator, a reason, the provider deadline passed, and either verified usage with evidence or ASSUME_MAX (the full reserve stays spent). Nothing releases it automatically, a reservation is recovered at most once, and there is no automatic retry.

Failed provider calls still consume one request. HTTP error responses and refusals settle at the reported usage. A timeout or transport error has unknown provider usage and settles at the full reserve.
RI_LAB_SPEND_GUARD_MODE=memory is for offline tests only. Live execution without a shared database fails closed.
A request that passes pre-flight may still consume thinking tokens inside max_tokens before text appears; partial responses may still incur billed input tokens.
No org-wide Anthropic workspace spend cap — only per-request guard when env is set.
Retries inside callAnthropicMessages are not implemented; retryReserveFactor reserves headroom only.
Provider errors after HTTP 200 may still bill input/output tokens reported by Anthropic.
